message.content: I'll stay in jail and roll rather than pay to leave. The first failed roll is free shelter, and leaving now just starts a lap into hotel rents I can't cover.
message.reasoning:
I need to choose between paying the $50 jail fine or rolling for doubles.

I'm weighing the $50 fine against rolling for doubles. I have $189 cash and zero jail turns, so I could sit through two more rolls. The main threat is p4's light blue hotels with hotels on Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut.

I own the pink monopoly, blocking p4's Virginia. p3 has brown hotels on Mediterranean and Baltic. p2 is broke with mortgaged railroads and zero houses on Boardwalk.

I own the orange set but New York is mortgaged so I cannot build there. I also own Water Works and Marvin Gardens. Paying the fine would drop my cash to $139 and force me to move immediately, starting a lap through dangerous properties. Rolling doubles is only a one-in-six chance, but it would let me leave and move normally.

I will roll for doubles to stay sheltered. I have not paid the fine yet.

p4 just landed on St Charles and paid me $10. They are extremely rich with $3,095. p2 is nearly bankrupt with only $5 but still holds dark blue properties unimproved. p3 has $395 and brown hotels.

The long-term problem is p4's dominance with $3,095 and light blue hotels.

I cannot trade during the jail decision, so rolling doubles is the only viable path. If I roll out of jail, I would land on St. Charles, States, Virginia, Penn RR, St. James, or Tennessee.

The exit roll from jail is actually safe. New York is mortgaged, so it yields no rent. Free Parking and Kentucky are also harmless.

The real danger is the next full lap through p4's light blue hotels and p3's brown hotels. Those can cost over $550 each. Staying in jail buys time to avoid that lethal circuit.
